 Ashramji Ashram

 Jaydeep H Sindhi(9585) for the Appellant(s) No. 1

sentences.text: 1. The present First Appeal, under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is preferred by the appellant - original opponent No.2 i.e. owner of the Truck, being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award dated 18.02.2009 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Main), Sabarkantha at Himmatnagar in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.612 of 2005, by which the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.1,48,300/- with 7.5% per annum interest to the claimant/s, holding Opponents No.1 & 2 i.e. driver and owner of the Truck bearing registration No.GJ-1-V-5935 liable, jointly and severally.

sentences.text:
It is noted that the Tribunal has dismissed the claim petition against NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2178/2024 ORDER DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined opponents No.4 and 5 i.e. driver and owner of Rickshaw bearing registration No.GJ1-TT-2531.
2.
Brief facts of the case, as per claimant/s, are as under :

vs Pravinbhai Mafatlal Shah on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60385980/
1 2.1

That on 13.01.2004 at about 8:00 p.m., the applicant / claimant was coming towards Geeta Mandir S.T. Stand at Ahmedabad in Rickshaw bearing registration No.GJ- 1-TT-2531, which was driven on correct side of Jamalpur - Geeta Mandir Road in Ahmedabad City.
When he reached at the place of accident, opponent No.1 - driver of the Truck bearing registration No.GJ-1-V-5935 came with full speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed with the said rickshaw.
As a result, the applicant sustained serious injuries.
Therefore, he has filed a claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.6 lakhs with cost and interest against the present respondents before the Tribunal.
2.2 Though served, Opponents No.1, 2, 4 and 5 i.e. all the opponents, have chosen not to appear and contest the claim petition before the Tribunal.
Opponent No.3 - Insurance Company is not known and therefore, the question of its appearing does not arise.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2178/2024 ORDER DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined
2.3 The Tribunal has framed the issues.

After considering the documentary evidence and submissions made at the bar by the claimant, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition by awarding compensation,
ex-parte, as noted above.

2.4 Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal,
the present appeal is preferred by the appellant - opponent No.2 i.e. owner of the Truck in question.

3. Learned advocate for the appellant/s - original opponent No.2 - owner of the Truck in question,
has submitted that the Tribunal has passed the impugned judgment and award ex-parte; and that the appellant was not given sufficient opportunity to lead evidence before the Tribunal; and that the offending truck was fully insured at the relevant time and therefore, there was no question of escaping from the proceedings before the Tribunal; and that the driver of the truck was also having valid driving license; and that the Tribunal has solely relying upon the submissions made by the claimant; and that sufficient opportunities may be given to the appellant to put his case before the Tribunal.

He has submitted that the matter may be remanded back to the Tribunal concerned for fresh NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2178/2024 ORDER DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined adjudication after giving proper opportunities to adduce and produce the relevant and necessary evidence, within reasonable time.
4. Learned advocate Ms. Krupa Soni for the respondent - original claimant has submitted that the Tribunal has rightly passed the impugned judgment and award.
She has submitted that the Tribunal has considered all the relevant documents available on record and allowed the claim petition.
She has submitted that notices were served to all the opponents, but they have not availed opportunity to represent their case.
She has submitted that the appellant has not deposited any amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal till date.

She has submitted that appropriate order of deposition and disbursement may be passed as the claimant is waiting for the fruits since long,
though the judgment and award is in his favour.
5.

The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act are benevolent legislation and normally, it should be construed that the provisions of the Act are enacted to see that the claimants could get some amount Ashramji Ashram vs Pravinbhai Mafatlal Shah on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60385980/
2 of compensation where the claimants either lose their bread-earner or has received serious injuries.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There cannot be any perfect arithmetic calculation for awarding amount of calculation.

Further,
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2178/2024 ORDER DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined considering Sections 166, 167 ad 168 of the Act, the object of the M.V. Act and the various judgments of the Hon'ble Apex Court whereby it is observed that the Court should try to give proper meaning to the provisions of the Act in such cases filed under the Act and such claim petitions, normally, should not be rejected by taking hyper technical view and if sufficient material is available on the record of the Tribunal or Court, the Tribunal shall consider the such claim petition/s on its own merits instead of dismissing such claim petition/s by taking hyper technical view and by asking for strict proof about the cause of the accident and involvement of the vehicle.
It is noteworthy to mention that the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 which gives paramount importance to the concept of 'just and fair' compensation.
The concept of 'just compensation' which ought to be determined on the foundation of fairness, reasonableness and equitability.
It also endeavors to make good the human suffering to the extent possible and to also save families which have lost their breadwinners from being pushed to wandering.

6. Under the circumstances, the ends of justice would meet, if the matter is required to be remanded back to the concerned Tribunal for fresh consideration, after giving proper NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2178/2024 ORDER DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined opportunities to the parties to adduce and produce the relevant and necessary evidence on record, within reasonable period, in accordance with law.

At the same time, it is required to be noted that the accident in question was of the year 2004, the claim petition is filed in the year 2005, the Tribunal has decided the claim petition in the year 2009,
the appeal is preferred by the appellant in the year 2024.
The concerned opponents have not deposited any money till date.

Therefore, almost about 20 years have been passed and the claimant,
who is a judgment creditor, is without the fruits of his legal battle after about two decades.
7. In view of above, the following order is passed.

7.1 The impugned judgment and award dated 18.02.2009 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Main), Sabarkantha at Himmatnagar in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.612 of 2005 is hereby quashed and set aside, on condition that the present appellant shall deposit principal award amount i.e. 1,48,300/-, round figure Rs.1,50,000/-, before the Tribunal concerned within a period of four weeks from today.

sentences.text: 7.2 The Tribunal concerned is hereby directed to decide the claim petition afresh, after giving proper NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2178/2024 ORDER DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined opportunities to the parties to adduce and produce the relevant and necessary evidence on record, as expeditiously as possible, in accordance with law.

7.3 Thereafter, the learned Tribunal shall disburse 50% amount to the original claimant, by account payee cheque/NEFT/RTGS, after following due procedure and invest the remaining 50% amount in non-cumulative Fixed Deposit Receipt in any nationalized bank, to be kept in custody of Nazir,
initially for a period of three years, and thereafter, renew the same periodically till further orders.

7.4 With above observation and direction, both these appeals are disposed of.
Notice is discharged.
7.5 The record and proceedings, if any, be sent back to the concerned Tribunal, forthwith.
8. In view of disposal of main appeal, civil application would not survive and is disposed of accordingly.
